work_order.understanding: A custom report's conditions button is icon-only. CompactFiltersButton renders a bare Button whose only child is SvgFilter, with no text node and no aria-label, so its accessible name is empty (CompactFiltersButton.tsx:8-14). The e2e page model works around that by enumerating every button in the report page, skipping any that carries an aria-label or non-empty text, and clicking the first whose bounding box sits right of x=850 (custom-report-page.ts:55-77). That is the only way the suite reaches the conditions menu, and it is actively fragile rather than merely untidy: the scan skips every NAMED button, so the moment the toolbar gains any named button it silently selects a different control. The fix is to give the button a name and address it by that name, which also retires the geometry. The second half of the ticket is the e2e file's own duplication: selectOnlyBillsGroup and switchToAnyOf each exist twice, byte-identical apart from a comment, so hoisting them is what makes the first change cheap. This is the fifth planning pass; the fourth rejection's single objection is answered point by point in debate_summary, and the shape of every criterion in acceptance[] is now either browser-observable or a named tests[] case that CI runs.
work_order.root_cause: The control has no accessible name, and the locator that had to compensate for that compensates with geometry. The x>850 threshold is a function of the fixed-width content to the button's left, not of viewport width: ReportTopbar renders nine GraphButtons, three 1px dividers and a SnapshotButton, all flexShrink: 0, then a SpaceBetween with flex:1, flexWrap:'nowrap' and justifyContent:'space-between' (ReportTopbar.tsx:227-233) whose first child is the compact FilterButton (ReportTopbar.tsx:234-235). Inside a space-between row the first child sits at the region's left edge, so narrowing the window pushes SaveReport right rather than moving the filter button left. What does follow from the code is that 850 is a fragile sum of sidebar widths with little slack, and that a control with no name cannot be addressed at all except by such a sum.
work_order.approach: Add aria-label={t('Filters')} to the existing bare Button in CompactFiltersButton, reusing the translation key the sibling tooltip on this very control already uses (FiltersMenu.tsx:744) and matching the pattern every other icon-only control in the topbar uses (GraphButton.tsx:42, SnapshotButton.tsx:40). An aria-label adds no rendered node, so no VRT snapshot moves. Then reduce openConditionsMenu to a single getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters', exact: true }).click(), which deletes the button scan, the hasName probe, the boundingBox call, the x>850 comparison and the now-unreachable throw, and hoist the two duplicated e2e helpers to the body of the 'custom reports' describe. Because no CI-executed check touches packages/desktop-client/e2e/ (.sdlc/config.yml:172 e2e is empty; vite.config.mts:406 vitest includes only src/**; desktop-client tsconfig.json:33 excludes e2e), the e2e suite is not a gate and is treated throughout as a local-only run in qa_script. Every criterion in acceptance[] is therefore either browser-observable at the live URL or names a case from tests[] that `yarn test` runs; no criterion asks a reader to grep a file, and the source-shape properties the fourth rejection objected to live in files[].why and tests[] where the diff reviewer reads them.

Nothing else changes: the SvgFilter child and its width/height/flexShrink, the minWidth, the bare variant and the onPress plumbing stay exactly as they are, and no text node is introduced.

'Filters' is already a translation key in this feature - the tooltip content on this same control at FiltersMenu.tsx:744 - so no new string enters the catalog and generate:i18n output is unaffected. aria-label rather than a visually-hidden span or a title attribute, because aria-label is the pattern the neighbouring icon-only toolbar buttons already use and it adds no DOM node, hence no layout shift and no VRT movement. The component library Button destructures restProps at Button.tsx:136 and spreads them onto the underlying react-aria Button at :169, so aria-label already reaches the DOM through that path in GraphButton and SnapshotButton and no plumbing is needed.

files.change: Replace the entire body of openConditionsMenu with one statement: `await this.pageContent.getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters', exact: true }).click();`. Delete the buttons/count loop, the hasName probe, the boundingBox() call, the box.x > 850 comparison and the unreachable throw at the end of the method. Rewrite the JSDoc at :50-54 to say the button is addressed by its accessible name rather than by its position among the topbar buttons. files.why: Once the control has a name, the geometric scan is not just fragile but actively harmful: it skips every named button, so it would silently pick a different control the moment the toolbar gains one. The rewritten body contains NO boundingBox call, NO coordinate comparison and NO loop over the page's buttons, and no try/catch or optional chaining either, so a control that cannot be found fails the click outright rather than falling through to a skip. exact:true keeps the compact and non-compact variants distinguishable - the accounts page's sibling is named 'Filter' (FiltersButton.tsx:13, used at account-page.ts:56) and Playwright's default name matching is substring-based. The tooltip's own 'Filters' text renders in a role="tooltip" element, which getByRole('button') cannot match, so the name is unique on the page.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts:651`

Evidence: The test body is a positive assertion only — `await customReportPage.openConditionsMenu(); await expect(page.getByTestId('filters-select-tooltip')).toBeVisible();` — and the work order's own root_cause states the reason: "The x>850 threshold is a function of the fixed-width content to the button's left, not of viewport width", i.e. narrowing 1280 -> 1024 leaves the button's x unchanged, so the pre-fix scan would still have satisfied x>850 at 1024px and still have opened the same popover. The pre-existing tests at reports.test.ts:326 and :461 already reach `filters-select-tooltip` under the same `beforeEach`, so the assertion proves nothing new about AC-3's locator. The only test in the PR that fails on the unfixed code is the vitest case in CompactFiltersButton.test.tsx; the e2e half of AC-3/AC-4 is guarded by nothing.

Fix: Either assert on the locator itself (e.g. expect the button matched by name to be the same node that opens the popover, or assert the accessible name is present), or state in the test comment that this is a smoke check at 1024px and not a regression test for the locator change — the comment currently explains the isNarrowWidth gate but not the coverage gap.

review.title: The JSDoc gives a reason for `exact: true` that cannot be the reason, and would mislead the next reader about how the locator is scoped.

The JSDoc gives a reason for `exact: true` that cannot be the reason, and would mislead the next reader about how the locator is scoped.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/custom-report-page.ts:54`

Evidence: The comment reads "`exact` keeps it distinct from the accounts page's sibling, which is named 'Filter'." But the locator is scoped to `this.pageContent`, which is `page.getByTestId('reports-page')` (custom-report-page.ts:14), and the accounts page is a different route with its own page model — `account-page.ts:56` is the only other Filter-named locator in e2e and it never runs against this page. The real reason `exact` is defensive: `FilterButton` renders `compact ? <CompactFiltersButton> : <FiltersButton>` (FiltersMenu.tsx:753), and FiltersButton renders `<Trans>Filter</Trans>`, so the two variants are mutually exclusive and can never both be present. Without `exact`, substring matching would also make `account-page.ts:56` match a 'Filters' name on any page that ever renders the compact variant.

Fix: Rewrite the sentence to state that `exact` guards against the singular 'Filter' sibling variant of the same control, and that the accounts-page mention concerns the other page model, not this locator.

review.title: No file under `upcoming-release-notes/` accompanies the PR, and the work order's out-of-scope reason ('alters no rendered output') does not hold for this change, which adds a user-visible accessible name.
review.detail:
No file under `upcoming-release-notes/` accompanies the PR, and the work order's out-of-scope reason ('alters no rendered output') does not hold for this change, which adds a user-visible accessible name.

Evidence: `git diff --name-status origin/main...FETCH_HEAD` lists four files and none under `upcoming-release-notes/`. `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:105` states "Add a release note. These notes get used when generating the full release note at the next release." and lists an `Enhancements` category at :129-134. The repository writes notes for changes smaller than this one, e.g. `upcoming-release-notes/clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md` (a comment rewrap) and `fix-e2e-long-note-flake.md`. Commit ede8c09 exists solely because a shipped custom-report fix went out without one. The change is user-facing to screen-reader users: before it, `CompactFiltersButton` had only `SvgFilter` (icons/v1/Filter.tsx renders one `<path>`, no text), so a screen reader announced an unnamed button; after it, it is announced as 'Filters'. Nothing renders differently visually, but the accessible name is a user-perceivable output.

Fix: Add a one-line note under `upcoming-release-notes/` (e.g. `name-compact-filter-button.md`, category `Enhancements` or `Bugfix`), or record in the PR why the accessibility change alone does not warrant one. Note that no check enforces this in this repository: `grep -rn "actions/release-notes\|release-notes/check" .github/` returns nothing, so the enforcing action is not wired into any workflow, and `packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-gate.mjs` (run by `yarn test`) only validates notes that already exist.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts:663`

Evidence: beforeEach at reports.test.ts:23-24 does page = await browser.newPage(), and afterEach at :35-37 closes that page, so each test() starts from a new context-sized page. playwright.config.ts sets no viewport in use, so every fresh page opens at the default 1280x720 regardless of what the previous test did. expect(screen.getByRole(...)).toBeDefined() is a tautology — getByRole already throws when nothing matches, so the assertion cannot fail — and it diverges from the assertion convention used everywhere else in this package.

`packages/desktop-client/src/components/filters/CompactFiltersButton.test.tsx:21`

Evidence: Across packages/desktop-client/src/**/*.test.tsx, toBeInTheDocument() appears in 20 files and toBeDefined() in 3 (TransactionsTable.test.tsx:812 on a dataset key, ManageTags.test.tsx:113,123 on a helper's return value). This line is the test that proves the fix — the one case that fails on the unfixed component.

Fix: Use expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters' })).toBeInTheDocument(); to match FiltersMenu.test.tsx and the rest of the package.

qa.title: Icon toolbar buttons announce their label twice: once as name, once as tooltip description
qa.expected: A control whose visible content is only an icon should announce its label once. Either the tooltip supplies the name (pre-PR behaviour for the Filters button) or aria-label supplies it, but not both at the same time.
qa.actual: GraphButton.tsx and SnapshotButton.tsx each render <Tooltip content={title}><Button aria-label={title}/></Tooltip>. React Aria's useTooltipTrigger sets 'aria-describedby' to the tooltip id whenever the tooltip is open (node_modules/react-aria/dist/private/tooltip/useTooltipTrigger.mjs:105), on hover and on keyboard focus alike, regardless of whether the trigger already has its own accessible name. Every icon button in the reports topbar therefore has an accessible description identical to its accessible name, and a screen reader says "Data Table, Data Table, button". This PR adds the Filters button to that set: it previously had no accessible name at all, and now has the name "Filters" plus the description "Filters".
repro: Open Reports and add a custom report.
Tab to the icon buttons in the topbar, or hover any of them.
Inspect the button: aria-label and the element referenced by aria-describedby carry the same string.
With a screen reader attached, the label is announced twice.
Before this PR the same inspection on "Data Table", "Show Legend" and "Download Snapshot" produced the identical result - the defect is the shared pattern, not this button.
qa.suspected_cause: The Tooltip-plus-aria-label pairing is a pre-existing convention in this codebase, not something this PR authored. git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD shows GraphButton.tsx and SnapshotButton.tsx untouched; both already paired aria-label with an identical Tooltip, and the same toolbar already announces "Data Table, Data Table" on main. This PR follows that convention for the Filters button rather than inventing it, so I am filing it as pre-existing and not blocking on it. The proper fix is one place, not here: drop the redundant Tooltip where the trigger already carries aria-label, or drop the aria-label and let the tooltip name the control. Doing that inside this PR would mean diverging from the convention its sibling buttons use, which is a wider change than issue #86 asked for.
